I've written the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, but I haven't compared it against the lodash original. The `lodash` package isn't installed here, so I couldn't run the original, and I can't print the original's bundle size either.

| Function | Before (lodash) | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `applyPatch` | `merge` | `merge` from `es-toolkit` (strict) | Strict `merge` merges arrays by index and keeps nested keys, as lodash does. On a sample with `a:[1,2,3]` and a patch of `a:[9]`, both strict and compat gave `[9,2,3]`. |
| `toTitle` | `startCase` | `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat` | Strict `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word. It gives `Http Server Id` where lodash gives `HTTP Server Id`, and `ABC-9x` becomes `Abc 9 X`. That would break the "consecutive capitals" inputs, so I used compat. |
| `preview` | `truncate` | `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat` | Strict has no `truncate`. A 30-character string came out as 21 characters plus `...`, which is what lodash does with `length: 24`. |

The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged. There is no hand-written replacement code and no lodash import. `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 2364 bytes (min+gzip), with 97 bytes of my own code.

Compat `startCase` and `truncate` make up most of that 2364 bytes. The strict `startCase` would be smaller, but it changes the output, so I kept compat.
